One parameter generalization of BW inequality and its application to open quantum dynamics

Dariusz Chruściński Email: darch@fizyka.umk.pl Address: Institute of Physics, Faculty of Physics, Astronomy and Informatics Nicolaus Copernicus University, Grudzia̧dzka 5/7, 87–100 Toruń, Poland    Gen Kimura Email: gen@shibaura-it.ac.jp Address: College of Systems Engineering and Science, Shibaura Institute of Technology, Saitama 330-8570, Japan    Hiromichi Ohno Email: h_ohno@shinshu-u.ac.jp Address: Department of Mathematics, Faculty of Engineering, Shinshu University, 4-17-1 Wakasato, Nagano 380-8553, Japan. Corresponding author: Corresponding author    Tanmay Singal Email: tanmaysingal@gmail.com Address: Institute of Physics, Faculty of Physics, Astronomy and Informatics Nicolaus Copernicus University, Grudzia̧dzka 5/7, 87–100 Toruń, Poland
Abstract

In this paper, we introduce a one parameter generalization of the famous Böttcher-Wenzel (BW) inequality in terms of a qq-deformed commutator. For n×nn\times n matrices AA and BB, we consider the inequality

Re⟨[B,A],[B,A]q⟩≤c⁡(q)​‖A‖2​‖B‖2,\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}\langle[B,A],[B,A]_{q}\rangle\leq c(q)\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2},

where ⟨A,B⟩=tr⁡(A∗​B)\langle A,B\rangle=\tr(A^*B) is the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product, ‖A‖\|A\| is the Frobenius norm, [A,B]=A​B−B​A[A,B]=AB-BA is the commutator, and [A,B]q=A​B−q​B​A[A,B]_{q}=AB-qBA is the qq-deformed commutator. We prove that when n=2n=2, or when AA is normal with any size nn, the optimal bound is given by

c⁡(q)=(1+q)+2​(1+q2)2.c(q)=\frac{(1+q)+\sqrt{2(1+q^{2})}}{2}.

We conjecture that this is also true for any matrices, and this conjecture is perfectly supported for nn up to 1515 by numerical optimization. When q=1q=1, this inequality is exactly BW inequality. When q=0q=0, this inequality leads the sharp bound for the rr-function which is recently derived for the application to universal constraints of relaxation rates in open quantum dynamics.

Keywords: 
Hilbert-Schmidt Inner Product, Frobenius Norm, Commutator, BW inequality,

1 Introduction

For any complex matrices A,B∈Mn​(ℂ)A,B\in M_{n}(\mathop{\mathbb{C}}\nolimits), the sharp bound for the norm of commutator is known:

‖[A,B]‖2≤2​‖A‖2​‖B‖2,\|[A,B]\|^{2}\leq 2\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2}, (1)

where [A,B]:=A​B−B​A[A,B]:=AB-BA denotes the commutator and the matrix norm is the Frobenius norm ‖A‖=tr⁡(A∗​A)\|A\|=\sqrt{\tr(A^*A)}. The inequality is often called the Böttcher-Wenzel (BW) inequality because of the following history: The inequality was first conjectured by Böttcher and Wenzel in [2] giving a proof for real 2×22\times 2 matrices and also for normal matrices. Later, Lásló proved BW inequality for 3×33\times 3 real matrices [12], Lu [13] and, independently, Wong and Jin [15] proved it for n×nn\times n real matrices, after which the complex case was proved by Böttcher and Wenzel in [3].

On the other hand, motivated by a problem in the field of open quantum systems [1], we have introduced the following real-valued functional in [4]:

r⁡(A,B)=12​(⟨[B,A],B​A⟩+⟨[B,A∗],B​A∗⟩)r(A,B)=\frac{1}{2}\left(\langle[B,A],BA\rangle+\langle[B,A^{*}],BA^{*}\rangle\right) (2)

for any A,B∈Mn​(ℂ)A,B\in M_{n}(\mathop{\mathbb{C}}\nolimits) where A∗A^{*} is the Hermitian conjugation of AA and ⟨A,B⟩=tr⁡(A∗​B)\langle A,B\rangle=\tr(A^*B) is the Hilbert-Schmidt inner product. The sharp bound for the rr-function was shown in [4]:

r⁡(A,B)≤1+22​‖A‖2​‖B‖2.r(A,B)\leq\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2}. (3)

This has been used to derive a universal constraint [6, 10, 11] for relaxation rates which is satisfied by any quantum Markovian dynamics described by completely positive dynamical semigroup, or GKLS master equation [7]. For this reason, we called the functional (2) the rr-function, where “rr” stands for relaxation.

In [4], we also observed a close relationship between BW inequality and inequality (3). If BB is normal, rr-function reduces to the commutator:

r⁡(A,B)=12​‖[A,B]‖2.r(A,B)=\frac{1}{2}\|[A,B]\|^{2}.

Hence, the direct application of BW inequality leads the bound

r⁡(A,B)≤‖A‖2​‖B‖2.r(A,B)\leq\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2}.

However, this is only true for a normal matrix BB and does not hold for general matrices. On the other hand, applying the triangle inequality, Schwarz inequality, the norm inequality ‖A​B‖≤‖A‖​‖B‖\|AB\|\leq\|A\|\|B\| and BW inequality for (2) implies the following general bound:

r⁡(A,B)≤2​‖A‖2​‖B‖2.r(A,B)\leq\sqrt{2}\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2}.

However, this in turn is a loose inequality. In the end, the sharp bound for general matrices is given by (3) and, therefore the relation between BW inequality and (3) is not yet fully understood.

The purpose of this paper is to provide one answer to this problem by introducing the following function (referred in this paper ff-function) for complex matrices A,B∈Mn​(ℂ)A,B\in M_{n}(\mathop{\mathbb{C}}\nolimits) and one parameter q∈ℝq\in\mathop{\mathbb{R}}\nolimits:

f⁡(A,B,q)\displaystyle f(A,B;q) :=Re⟨[B,A],[B,A]q⟩\displaystyle:=\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}\langle[B,A],[B,A]_{q}\rangle
=tr⁡(A∗​B∗​B​A+q​B∗​A∗​A​B−1+q2​(A∗​B∗​A​B+B∗​A∗​B​A)),\displaystyle=\tr\left(A^{\mathrm{\ast}}B^{\mathrm{\ast}}BA+qB^{\mathrm{\ast}}A^{\mathrm{\ast}}AB-\frac{1+q}{2}(A^{\mathrm{\ast}}B^{\mathrm{\ast}}AB+B^{\mathrm{\ast}}A^{\mathrm{\ast}}BA)\right), (4)

where [A,B]q:=A​B−q​B​A[A,B]_{q}:=AB-qBA is the qq-deformed commutator [8, 14]. When q=1q=1, the ff-function is exactly the norm squared of the commutator:

f⁡(A,B,1)=‖[A,B]‖2.f(A,B;1)=\|[A,B]\|^{2}. (5)

(See also [5] for another generalization ‖[A,B]q‖2\|[A,B]_{q}\|^{2} and its norm bound.) When q=0q=0, the ff-function and rr-function have the following relation:

r⁡(A,B)=f⁡(A,B,0)+f⁡(A∗,B,0)2.r(A,B)=\frac{f(A,B;0)+f(A^{\mathrm{\ast}},B;0)}{2}. (6)

In this sense, the ff-function connects the rr-function and the norm squared of the commutator through one parameter qq.

We consider the sharp bound for the ff-function, and obtain a partial answer.

Theorem 1

Let AA and BB be n×nn\times n complex matrices. If AA is a normal matrix or n=2n=2, then the inequality

f⁡(A,B,q)≤c⁡(q)​‖A‖2​‖B‖2f(A,B;q)\leq c(q)\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2} (7)

holds, where

c⁡(q)=(1+q)+2​(1+q2)2.c(q)=\frac{(1+q)+\sqrt{2(1+q^{2})}}{2}.

Moreover, this inequality is sharp, i.e., there are non-zero matrices AA and BB at which the bound is attained.

We conjecture that the theorem is also true for any matrices A,B∈Mn​(ℂ)A,B\in M_{n}(\mathop{\mathbb{C}}\nolimits). This is numerically supported for nn up to 1515 (See Fig. 1).

Importantly, the inequality (7) integrates BW inequality and the inequality (3) as follows. First, inequality (7) with q=1q=1 recovers BW inequality by noting c⁡(1)=2c(1)=2 and using relation (5). Hence, inequality (7) is considered as a one-parameter generalization of BW inequality. Second, when q=0q=0, we have c⁡(0)=1+22c(0)=\frac{1+\sqrt{2}}{2}, and therefore, (7) and (6) imply inequality (3) for rr-function. We also note that, the conjecture (7) for q=−1q=-1 is easily shown by noting c⁡(−1)=1c(-1)=1 and f⁡(A,B,−1)=‖B​A‖2−‖A​B‖2f(A,B;-1)=\|BA\|^{2}-\|AB\|^{2} and using the norm inequality ‖B​A‖≤‖B‖​‖A‖\|BA\|\leq\|B\|\|A\|.

2.2 Proof for normal matrix

In this subsection, the proof of Theorem 1 for normal matrix is given. Suppose that AA is a normal matrix. By the unitary invariance of the ff-function, we can assume that AA is a diagonal matrix. Letting A=diag⁡[a1,a2,…,an]A={\rm diag}[a_{1},a_{2},\ldots,a_{n}] and B=(bi​j)B=(b_{ij}), direct computation shows ‖A‖2=∑i|ai|2,‖B‖2=∑i,j|bj​i|2\|A\|^{2}=\sum_{i}|a_{i}|^{2},\|B\|^{2}=\sum_{i,j}|b_{ji}|^{2} and

f⁡(A,B,q)=∑i≠j|bj​i|2​(|ai|2+q​|aj|2−(1+q)​Re(ai​aj¯)).f(A,B;q)=\sum_{i\neq j}|b_{ji}|^{2}(|a_{i}|^{2}+q|a_{j}|^{2}-(1+q)\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}(a_{i}\overline{a_{j}})).

Hence, we have

c​‖A‖2​‖B‖2−f⁡(A,B,q)\displaystyle c\|A\|^{2}\|B\|^{2}-f(A,B;q)
≥∑i≠j|bj​i|2​(c⁡(∑k|ak|2)−|ai|2−q​|aj|2+(1+q)​Re(ai​aj¯))\displaystyle\geq\sum_{i\neq j}|b_{ji}|^{2}(c(\sum_{k}|a_{k}|^{2})-|a_{i}|^{2}-q|a_{j}|^{2}+(1+q)\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}(a_{i}\overline{a_{j}}))
OPEN≥∑i≠j|bj​i|2​((c−1)​|ai|2)+(c−q)​|aj|2+(1+q)​Re(ai​aj¯))\displaystyle\geq\sum_{i\neq j}|b_{ji}|^{2}((c-1)|a_{i}|^{2})+(c-q)|a_{j}|^{2}+(1+q)\mathop{\mathrm{Re}}(a_{i}\overline{a_{j}}))
=∑i≠j|bj​i|2​|c−1​ai+ε1​c−q​aj|2≥0,\displaystyle=\sum_{i\neq j}|b_{ji}|^{2}|\sqrt{c-1}a_{i}+\varepsilon_{1}\sqrt{c-q}a_{j}|^{2}\geq 0,

where in the equality we have used Lemma 1. Therefore, the bound (7) is shown for a normal matrix AA where BB is any complex matrix.

One can prove that the inequality is sharp using the same example in the proof for n=2n=2. ■\blacksquare

3 Conclusion and discussion

In this paper, we have introduced the ff-function (4) which is a one parameter generalization of the norm square of the commutator and also rr-function. The conjectured bound (7) for the ff-function integrates BW inequality and our previously obtained inequality (3). The conjecture is numerically supported for nn up to 1515, and is proved when one of the matrix is normal, or for general 2×22\times 2 matrices.
